newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia coffee prices firm on tight supply.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia coffee prices firm on tight supply.

text.p: Indonesian coffee prices were firm on Monday on the back of tight supply in the domestic market, traders said.
"The domestic factor seems to be playing a bigger role in determining local prices," one trader in Sumatra said, adding local prices did not react to a softer London market.
He said offshore prices had been weak but local prices remained stable, with grade four export prices quoted at $1,550 a tonne fob Lampung in South Sumatra.
The trader said coffee traders were trapped between local tight supply and weak offshore prices.
"You can't pay higher prices for farmers because London prices cap the upside. But if you are ready to pay higher prices, you can't find enough supply," the trader said.
"We are in a real dilemma. This year has been difficult for us," the trader said, adding that the coffee crop was estimated to fall by about 40 percent from last year.
